cards.text: It's the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede, made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans. Daniel, a man of Judah carried off to Babylon, tells this part himself: he's reading the sacred books, and he comes to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet about Jerusalem's desolation. And friend, this man is doing the MATH.

cards.question: In the word of the LORD to Jeremiah, how long would the desolation of Jerusalem last?
So Daniel turns his attention to the Lord God, to seek Him by prayer and petition. What else does Daniel bring with him?

answers.text: A feast with music and dancing

cards.text: Then Daniel prays, and before he asks for ANYTHING, he starts with who God is: the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments. Friend, I open every phone call with "Hey, so, quick favor."

cards.question: When Daniel confesses, he talks about the people's sin but leaves himself out of it.

cards.text: Daniel says WE: we sinned, we did wrong, we acted wickedly, we rebelled. Friend, when the boss asks who jammed the copier, NOBODY says we.

cards.question: Daniel says they didn't listen to God's servants the ___, who spoke in His name to their kings, leaders, fathers and all the people.

cards.text: Daniel says righteousness belongs to God, but shame covers the people: the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in every country God drove them to because of their unfaithfulness. Their kings, leaders and fathers too, friend, so nobody's sneaking out the side door on this one.

cards.question: The people are covered with shame. But Daniel says something belongs to God, even though they rebelled against Him. What is it?

cards.text: No excuses, no "well, technically": Daniel says they didn't obey the voice of the LORD or walk in His laws, so the oath and the curse have been poured out on them.

cards.question: Daniel says the oath and the curse poured out on them were written in the Law of ___.

cards.text: Daniel says God has carried out the words spoken against them by bringing a great disaster, and under ALL of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what's been done to Jerusalem. Not once, friend, NOWHERE.

cards.question: After all that disaster, Daniel says the people turned from their iniquities and sought the favor of the LORD.

cards.text: Daniel says the LORD kept the calamity in store and brought it upon them. For the LORD is righteous in all He does, yet they haven't obeyed His voice.

cards.question: Daniel reminds God how He brought His people out of the land of ___ with a mighty hand.

cards.text: After ALL that confessing, now Daniel asks: that God's anger and wrath would turn away from His city Jerusalem, His holy mountain, and that God would cause His face to shine upon His desolate sanctuary. Friend, that's me on the phone with the bank: "Yep, I missed the payment, that's ALL on me... any chance you could waive the fee?"

cards.question: Daniel is honest about why he's asking. What does Daniel say his petitions rest on?
At the end of his prayer, Daniel asks God not to delay.

cards.text: "O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act!" That's not a polite little prayer, friend. That's a man asking with everything he's got, because God's city and God's people bear His name.

Daniel is STILL praying, still confessing his own sin and the sin of his people Israel, still bringing his petition about God's holy mountain. Friend, my prayers usually wrap up when the oven timer dings.

cards.question: While Daniel is still praying, ___ comes to him in swift flight, the man Daniel had seen in the earlier vision.

cards.text: Gabriel arrives about the time of the evening sacrifice, and he finds Daniel still praying. Friend, show up during MY evening prayers and you'll find me snoring before the amen.

cards.question: Gabriel tells Daniel why he's come. What is Gabriel here to give Daniel?
Gabriel says an answer to Daniel's prayer went out at the beginning of his petitions.

cards.text: Gabriel also tells Daniel he is highly precious, and friend, I came with a price sticker that said 25 cents. Then comes the message: seventy weeks are decreed for Daniel's people and his holy city.

cards.question: Seventy weeks are decreed for Daniel's people and holy city. What does Gabriel say they are decreed to do?

answers.text: Bring down the king of Persia
Send the people back to Egypt

cards.text: And there's more on that list: stop their transgression, make atonement for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up vision and prophecy, and anoint the Most Holy Place. Friend, my to-do list today says scrub the oven, and I'm already behind.

cards.question: Gabriel gives a starting point: the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem. Counting from there, who does Gabriel count up to?

cards.text: From the decree until the Messiah, the Prince, Gabriel counts seven weeks and sixty-two weeks, and Jerusalem will be rebuilt with streets and a trench. Daniel came in doing math, friend, and Gabriel brought him MORE math.

cards.question: Gabriel says Jerusalem will be rebuilt in peaceful and easy times.
After the sixty-two weeks, what does Gabriel say will happen to the Messiah?

answers.text: He will be cut off and have nothing
He will rule from the city of Babylon
He will be crowned in the citadel of Susa

cards.question: Gabriel says the people of the prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary.

cards.text: Lean in, friend: the end will come like a flood, and until the end there will be war, with desolations decreed. Then Gabriel speaks of someone he leaves unnamed, who will confirm a covenant with many for one week.

cards.question: Gabriel speaks of someone he leaves unnamed, who will confirm a covenant with many for one week. In the middle of that week, what will this one put an end to?

cards.text: Gabriel's last words: "And on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him." That's where his message ends, friend, and it's a heavy one.

findings.problem: The description of Daniel as a man of Judah carried off to Babylon is background from Daniel 1, not Daniel 9:1-2. It is useful background, but no reference accompanies that outside fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate this stop. Cards 2, 4, 5, 9, 12 and 13 ask for unrevealed details that cannot be inferred from the earlier cards: Gabriel's name, what he gives Daniel, when the answer went out, the endpoint of the timeline, what happens to the Messiah, and whether the coming prince's people destroy the city and sanctuary. That is six of the stop's nine choice cards, leaving most picks dependent on luck or prior knowledge rather than reasoning from the walkthrough.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
